div.head: Norðleoda 3
div.ab: Episcopi et aldermanni octo milia þrimsa.
Bisceopes and ealdermannes, VIII þusend þrymsa.
eines Bischofs und Ealdorman 8000 Tremissen [100 Pfund],
of a bishop and an ealdorman 8,000 thrymsas [100 pounds],
That of a bishop and an ealdorman 8,000 thrymsas.
For a bishop and an ealdorman, eight thousand thrymsas.
div.note: and ‘ðrymsa’ corrected to H's ‘þrymsa’. Liebermann compares the Instituta Cnuti III 57: ‘Episcopus et comes habent … leges equales’.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 12 / 13, October 2026 (was “eleventhcentury”, now “eleventh-century”)

ealdorman: A royal appointee charged with overseeing portions of the kingdom. Within the political hierarchy of early eleventh-century England, ealdormen were considered of higher rank than a reeve but below that of members of the royal family. The ealdorman’s responsibilities included presiding over courts, levying taxes, and supplying soldiers at the king’s request.

note.seg: ebd. 57: Episcopus et comes habent . . . leges ęquales
ibid. 57: Episcopus et comes habent . . . leges ęquales

Bischof und Ealdorman stehen auch sonst gleich; s. Gl Stand 19. 20a. 21d. e. f. i. l. p. r. Die Ansätze in 3—5 verhalten sich wie 4 : 2 : 1, dagegen die vor- und nachher ergeben Brüche. Jene Wergelder scheinen beeinflusst vom Norweg. Gulathingsrecht; Maurer Höldar 189. 198 ff.; Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 28

Bishop and ealdorman are equal elsewhere too; see Gl Stand 19. 20a. 21d. e. f. i. l. p. r. The assessments in 3—5 stand in the ratio 4 : 2 : 1, whereas those before and after yield fractions. Those wergilds seem to be influenced by the Norwegian Gulathing law; Maurer Höldar 189. 198 ff.; Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 28
